title: Letter 3 — On Faith and Works
attribution_note: Letter 3 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance. Part of the four-letter treatise On Faith (Letters 2–5); see Letter 2's note.

pairs.en: It is certainly necessary for whoever wants to be saved to hold Orthodoxy, or the right faith. But this alone is not sufficient for salvation. *“For the devils also believe, and tremble,”* in the apostle's words. [James 2:19] They believe that God is one, that Christ has come into the world, and they fear His holy name. Therefore the apostle demands that we show our faith by our works: *“Show me thy faith by thy works.”* [James 2:18] For as a good tree is known by good fruit, so a true and heartfelt faith is known by good works. Many are called faithful Christians, but their works show otherwise; they show faith with their lips, but by their works appear as pagans, or even worse than pagans: *“they profess that they know God; but in works they deny”* Him. [Titus 1:16] Therefore Orthodoxy must be joined to a living faith as well, which is always followed by works to match it. Strive to have such a faith, and you will be saved.
